'''Peter McMullen''' (born 11 May 1942)<ref>[http://www.dmg.tuwien.ac.at/gruber/gruber_arbeiten/mcmullen.pdf Peter McMullen], [[Peter M. Gruber]], retrieved 2013-11-03.</ref> is a British mathematician, a professor emeritus of mathematics at [[University College London]].<ref>[https://iris.ucl.ac.uk/iris/browse/profile?upi=PMCMU56 UCL IRIS information system], accessed 2013-11-05.</ref>

==Education and career==
McMullen earned bachelor's and master's degrees from [[Trinity College, Cambridge]], and studied at the [[University of Birmingham]], where he received his doctorate in 1968.<ref>{{citation
| last1 = McMullen | first1 = Peter
| last2 = Schulte | first2 = Egon
| title = Abstract and regular polytopes
| date = 12 December 2002
| publisher = Cambridge University Press
| isbn = 9780521814966
| url = https://books.google.com/books?id=JfmlMYe6MJgC&pg=PA530
| access-date= 2022-05-11
}}</ref>
He taught at [[Western Washington University]] from 1968 to 1969.<ref>[http://beta.worldcat.org/archivegrid/data/55804571 Peter McMullen Collection, 1967-1968], Special Collections, Wilson Library, Western Washington University, retrieved from worldcat.org 2013-11-03.</ref> In 1978 he earned his Doctor of Science at [[University College London]] where he still works as a professor emeritus. In 2006 he was accepted as a corresponding member of the Austrian Academy of Sciences.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.oeaw.ac.at/m/mcmullen-peter| title=Austrian Academy of Sciences: Peter McMullen| access-date=2022-05-11}}</ref>

==Contributions==
McMullen is known for his work in [[polyhedral combinatorics]] and [[discrete geometry]], and in particular for proving what was then called the upper bound conjecture and now is the [[upper bound theorem]]. This result states that [[cyclic polytope]]s have the maximum possible number of faces among all polytopes with a given dimension and number of vertices.<ref>{{citation|title=Lectures on Polytopes|volume=152|series=Graduate Texts in Mathematics|first=Günter M.|last=Ziegler|authorlink=Günter M. Ziegler|publisher=Springer|year=1995|isbn=9780387943657|page=254|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xd25TXSSUcgC&pg=PA254|quotation=Finally, in 1970 McMullen gave a complete proof of the upper-bound conjecture – since then it has been known as the upper bound theorem. McMullen's proof is amazingly simple and elegant, combining to key tools: shellability and ''h''-vectors.}}</ref> McMullen also formulated the g-conjecture, later the [[g-theorem]] of [[Louis Billera]], Carl W. Lee, and [[Richard P. Stanley]], characterizing the [[f-vector|''f''-vectors]] of [[simplicial sphere]]s.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Gruber | first = Peter M.
 | isbn = 978-3-540-71132-2
 | location = Berlin
 | mr = 2335496
 | page = 265
 | publisher = Springer
 | series = Grundlehren der Mathematischen Wissenschaften [Fundamental Principles of Mathematical Sciences]
 | title = Convex and discrete geometry
 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=bSZKAAAAQBAJ&pg=PA265
 | volume = 336
 | year = 2007|quotation=The problem of characterizing the ''f''-vectors of convex polytopes is ... far from a solution, but there are important contributions towards it. For simplicial convex polytopes a characterization was proposed by McMullen in the form of his celebrated ''g''-conjecture. The ''g''-conjecture was proved by Billera and Lee and Stanley}}.</ref>

The [[McMullen problem]] is an unsolved question in discrete geometry named after McMullen, concerning the number of points in [[general position]] for which a [[projective transformation]] into [[convex position]] can be guaranteed to exist. It was credited to a private communication from McMullen in a 1972 paper by David G. Larman.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Larman | first = D. G.
 | doi = 10.1112/blms/4.1.6
 | journal = The Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society
 | mr = 307040
 | pages = 6–12
 | title = On sets projectively equivalent to the vertices of a convex polytope
 | volume = 4
 | year = 1972}}</ref>

He is also known for his 1960s drawing, by hand, of a 2-dimensional representation of the Gosset polytope [[4 21 polytope|4<sub>21</sub>]], the vertices of which form the vectors of the [[E8_(mathematics)|E8 root system]].<ref>{{cite web
|url=https://aimath.org/E8/mcmullen.html 
|title=A picture of the E8 root system
|publisher=American Institute of Mathematics
|access-date=May 11, 2022}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
McMullen was invited to speak at the 1974 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Vancouver]]; his contribution there had the title ''Metrical and combinatorial properties of convex polytopes''.<ref>[http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM1974.1/Main/icm1974.1.0491.0496.ocr.pdf ICM 1974 proceedings] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171204061317/http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM1974.1/Main/icm1974.1.0491.0496.ocr.pdf |date=2017-12-04 }}.</ref>

He was elected as a foreign member of the [[Austrian Academy of Sciences]] in 2006.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20131104104357/http://www.ucl.ac.uk/news/people/june_2006|title=Awards, Appointments, Elections & Honours}}, University College London, June 2006, retrieved 2013-11-03.</ref> In 2012 he became an inaugural [[fellow]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of AMS fellows], retrieved 2013-11-03.</ref>
